ranking.note: Raised P3->P2: it is the stated prerequisite for P2 #34374 and corrects misleading public API semantics before stabilization, so it cannot sit below what it unblocks; moved up from position 11 for the same reason.

Raised P4->P3 and moved up from position 15: the summary describes a substantial decoupling of index code from node internals that fixes startup races and is a stated prerequisite for #10102 and #15719, which is more than cleanup.
Moved down from position 8: an opt-in, compile-time-disabled diagnostic ranks below the error-propagation, logging-boundary and multiprocess-decoupling work in the same band.
Lowered P3->P4: removal of two redundant accessors already covered by height lookups is cosmetic API polish with no consumer asking for it, per the category rule.

inconsistencies: Competing logging designs: #34775 makes the kernel logging callback global and deletes the connection handles, while #33847 attaches logging options to per-connection handles and #30342 hands out per-instance Logger objects. These cannot all land as designed; a decision is needed. Review #34775 first (it is the smallest statement of the question and gates #34374), then decide whether #33847/#30342 still apply.
Chain order: #34775 -> #34374 (structured log entries build on the simplified global callback); and #33847 is described as paving the way for #30342. Reviewing the dependents first will waste effort.

Overlapping problem: #29700 (return util::Result/FlushResult on all fatal errors) and #35646 (remove M_ERROR from ValidationState via util::Expected) both untangle fatal runtime errors from validation state. Review #29700 first as the broader, embedder-facing version, and treat #35646's kernel::FatalError type as the design question to settle jointly rather than twice.

#24230's stand-alone rationale ("only deletes unused block information definitions", "minor internal cleanup") contradicts its own summary (extracts sync into node::SyncChain, drops cs_main during sync, prerequisite for #10102/#15719). The band was set from the weaker reading.
External dependency noted on the card: #29700 requires base PR #25665 for extended util::Result support, which is outside this category.

Scope/splitting flags: #32427 rewrites the block tree storage layer (WAL + checksums) and #35187 adds a coin-fetch callback path through block validation; both are kernel-API work that also substantively changes validation/storage internals and may warrant splitting per the category note. #33117 is interfaces::Node / multiprocess-GUI plumbing rather than the kernel C API, so its fit in this category is weak.
result.notes: Four of the fifteen PRs are logging-boundary work by two authors pulling in opposite directions; the category's review capacity is better spent settling that design than on any single one of them. The clear P2 core is the work that decides whether external consumers can build on the library at all (concurrent readers, error propagation, validation without a UTXO set, build isolation, deterministic clock); everything below is polish, diagnostics, or accessor completeness.
